case_name: Vijay Kumar Ramachandra Bhate vs Neela Vijay Kumar Bhate
facts_of_case: The wife filed a petition for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1)(i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The husband lost before both courts below and appealed to challenge the orders.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the petitioner to establish his or her plea that the respondent had meted out cruelty.
legal_principles.held: normally the burden lies on the petitioner to establish his or her plea that the respondent had meted out cruelty and that the standard of proof required in matrimonial cases under the Act is not to establish the charge of cruelty beyond reasonable doubt but merely one of weighing the various probabilities to find out whether the preponderance is in favour of the existence of the said fact alleged.
cited_cases: Dr. N.G. Dastane v. Mrs. S. Dastane, AIR (1975) SC 1534

legal_principles.principle: Mental cruelty can broadly be defined as that conduct which inflicts upon the other party such mental pain and suffering as would make it not possible for that party to live with the other.
legal_principles.held: mental cruelty in Section 13(1) (i-a) can broadly be defined as that conduct which inflicts upon the other party such mental pain and suffering as would make it not possible for that party to live with the other and the parties cannot reasonably also be expected to live together or that the wronged party cannot reasonably be asked to put up with such conduct and continue to live with the other party.
cited_cases: V. Bhagat v. D. Bhagat (Mrs.), [1994] 1 SCC 337

outcome.final_order: The final court order granted dissolution of marriage and divorce on the ground of cruelty.
